title: The Vanished Star
subtitle: A Color By Number Mystery
setting: Larkspur Hollow is a small riverside town. Every winter its nine best-known neighbours help to raise a golden star onto the fir tree in the square. This year the star disappeared the night before the Lantern Festival.
intro: You are the town's volunteer detective. Each chapter hides one fact inside a colour-by-number mosaic. Colour it, read the symbol, and the evidence card tells you what it means.

chapters.title: A Thread on the Fir
chapters.story:
On the morning before the Lantern Festival, the great star was gone from the top of the square's fir tree. Caught on the highest branch was a single woollen thread.
Mayor Alder asked you to look closer. What colour was it? The mosaic remembers.
chapters.scene: Snowy town square at dawn, a tall fir tree with an empty top, a thread caught on a branch
chapters.meaning: The thread is red or blue. Whoever took the star did not wear a green scarf.

decoys.meaning: The thread is green. The taker wore a green scarf.
The thread is yellow. It came from the festival bunting, not from a scarf.

chapters.title: Clear Eyes in the Dark
chapters.story:
The lamplighter's ledger says the square was pitch dark at midnight. The baker's boy saw a figure reading the tiny brass label on the star without holding it close.
Someone who needs spectacles could not have done that.
chapters.scene: A brass label on a golden star, lantern light, a child peeking from a bakery window
chapters.meaning: The label was read from arm's length in the dark. The taker does not wear glasses.

decoys.meaning: The figure held the label right up to thick glasses.
The figure could not read the label at all and asked for help.

chapters.title: Prints in the Snow
chapters.story:
Fresh snow fell at eleven. By morning one clear trail crossed the square to the fir tree: deep, ridged prints.
The cobbler measured them with a ribbon and smiled.
chapters.scene: Boot prints crossing fresh snow toward a fir tree, a cobbler kneeling with a ribbon
chapters.meaning: The prints were made by heavy winter boots. The taker wore boots.

decoys.meaning: The prints were made by soft indoor slippers.
The prints were made by wooden skates.

chapters.title: The Frozen Bridge
chapters.story:
Only one bridge joins the two halves of the town, and the ferryman swears it was iced shut from dusk till dawn.
The trail of prints never came near the river.
chapters.scene: A small stone bridge covered in ice at night, a river, warm windows on the north bank
chapters.meaning: Nobody crossed the river that night. The taker lives on the north side.

decoys.meaning: The trail came over the bridge from the south side.
The trail came down from the eastern hill, outside the town.

chapters.title: Two Marks in the Bark
chapters.story:
Near the foot of the fir, two neat dents showed where something had leaned against the trunk. The dents were as wide apart as the rails of a ladder.
The star hung far too high to reach from the ground.
chapters.scene: Close view of a fir trunk with two dents in the snow-dusted bark, a ladder shadow
chapters.meaning: A ladder stood against the tree. The taker owns a ladder.

decoys.meaning: Someone climbed the branches. No ladder was used.
A long hook pole pulled the star down from the ground.

chapters.title: The Midnight Rehearsal
chapters.story:
From ten until one, the choir practised carols in the chapel. The choirmaster keeps a roll, and every singer on it was counted at the stroke of midnight.
The star vanished at midnight.
chapters.scene: A candle-lit chapel with a choir singing, a roll book on a stand, a clock showing midnight
chapters.meaning: Every choir member was in the chapel at midnight. The taker was not at choir practice.

decoys.meaning: The choir finished early, so any singer could have been in the square.
Three singers slipped out before midnight.

chapters.title: The Knot
chapters.story:
The rope that once held the star was still tied to the top branch. The sailor who taught knots at the school studied it for a long time.
A knot shows which hand tied it.
chapters.scene: A rope knot on a fir branch, an old sailor examining it with a magnifying glass
chapters.meaning: The knot was untied by a right-handed person. The taker is not left-handed.

decoys.meaning: The knot was untied by a left-handed person.
The rope was cut, so the knot says nothing.

chapters.title: No Whiskers Here
chapters.story:
Last of all, the baker's boy found a tuft of fur by the tree. The vet looked at it under her lamp: coarse, short and brown.
Not one cat hair lay anywhere on the trail.
chapters.scene: A vet with a lamp examining a tuft of brown fur, a friendly dog waiting by the door
chapters.meaning: No cat hair was found on the trail. The taker does not keep a cat.

decoys.meaning: Cat hair covered the rope. The taker keeps a cat.
The fur came from a fox that passed in the night.

finale: Eight facts, nine neighbours. Go through your Code Log and cross out everyone who does not fit a fact. One name stays.
epilogue: The star was never stolen. One of its points had cracked, and a kind neighbour carried it home at midnight to mend it in secret before the festival. By evening it shone on the fir tree again, brighter than before.
